title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-04-12
lineage: [SBD > Reel master > Sonic Solutions > DAT ] + [Aud > cassette master > PCM > DAT > Sonic Solutions] > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard capture of a fiery 1970 set highlighted by a scorching “Dancin’ in the Streets” and soaring Viola Lee Blues.
ai_review.review: The recording, taken from a well‑mixed 16‑track soundboard, delivers clear, present audio with only minor annoyances like occasional three‑second gaps between tracks. Musically the show is a standout of the era – Jerry’s “snaky” guitar work on a blistering Dancin’, a thunderous Viola Lee Blues, deep‑grooving Deep Elem and a soulful Black Peter make this one of the better 1970 performances. While a few transitions (notably China > Rider) feel sloppy and some listeners dislike the track pauses, the overall flow is tight and the band sounds inspired by the co‑headlining Miles Davis night.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (30+) are 4‑5 stars praising both performance and sound; only a few low scores focus on minor technical annoyances, yielding an overall high rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear mix with strong presence and balance (16‑track SBD). Minor issues: occasional 3‑second gaps between tracks, a few patch noises, but overall very listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Generally praised for smooth pacing; candyman → Viola Lee flow noted as especially seamless. The only disruption mentioned is the artificial 3‑second pauses between tracks.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as ‘snaky’, blazing, and uniquely creative on Dancin' with a standout solo that drives the jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: Solid, pounding bass throughout; highlighted for his contribution to the Dancin' groove and occasional pre‑Mind Left Body jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ (Pigpen) unusually forward in the mix, adding weight to Viola Lee and Dancin'; keyboards noted as more prominent than typical 1970 tapes.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drum break highlighted as a high point; overall tight rhythmic foundation supporting the extended jams.
